items.text: No pawns left? Go get theirs! They have been keeping them far too long.
Our last pawn! Right. New plan: take every pawn they have.
We are out of pawns, but they are not. I think you know what to do.
All our little heroes are gone. Make those fancy pieces earn their keep. Go hunt some pawns!
Not a single pawn left. I am taking this personally. Get theirs!
We may be out of pawns, but we are not out of pawn-taking opportunities. Keep looking!
Our little pawn took a big piece! Tell me again which pieces are important.
That is pawn power! Small piece, enormous ambition.
A pawn just punched above its weight. Beautiful work!
All that fancy equipment, defeated by a pawn. I love this game.
Look what our pawn brought home! That little fellow deserves a medal.
Who needs a bigger piece? Our pawn seems perfectly qualified.
Your pawn is threatening a bigger piece! Small but terrifying. I approve.
Look at that pawn bossing the big pieces around. That is leadership!
Our pawn has expensive taste. It is eyeing a much bigger piece.
A little pawn, a big threat. Never underestimate the little ones.
That bigger piece has a pawn problem. Excellent placement!
Make way for the pawn! Suddenly the fancy pieces look nervous.
Your queen for their pawn? Brilliant trade. You got the important piece!
They took the queen, but we got a pawn. That is a deal I would make all day.
A whole queen invested in one lovely pawn. Finally, someone understands value!
Let them celebrate the queen. We have the pawn. Excellent business.
You traded our pawn for a bigger piece? Bad trade. I wanted to keep the pawn!
Yes, you got a fancy piece. But we lost a pawn to do it! Those priorities need work.
A bigger piece is no consolation for that pawn. Next time, make the trade the other way around.
We gave up a perfectly good pawn for that? I would like a refund.
We gave up a big piece and brought home a pawn. Now that is a trade!
A fine exchange. They can keep the fancy piece. We got the pawn.
That piece has served its purpose: it got us a pawn. Excellent work.
A pawn for a pawn. I am pleased and upset in exactly equal amounts.
We got their pawn, but they got ours. Next time, can we just do the first part?
One pawn in, one pawn out. This collection is not going to grow itself.
They moved that pawn and you took it straight away. Excellent service!
A freshly delivered pawn! You did not keep it waiting. I like that.
Their pawn stepped forward, and you collected it. Beautiful timing.
A queen? There was a pawn right there! Bad move. You got distracted by the fancy hat.
You took the queen and left the pawn? I cannot approve of those priorities. Get the pawn!
You traded a perfectly good pawn opportunity for a queen? I expected better.
That queen capture looked flashy. Taking the pawn would have looked better to me.
Why the queen? The pawn was available. We have discussed this!
You got the big piece and missed the little one. That is the wrong way around.
You took a piece, but you could have taken a pawn. Bad choice. The pawn was the prize!
A stronger piece? Sure. A better choice than the pawn? Not in my book.
You could have taken a pawn, but you went for the fancy piece instead. Disappointing.
That capture had everything except the one thing I wanted: the pawn you left behind.
I saw the pawn capture. You saw the bigger piece. One of us needs to reconsider.
You missed an opportunity to take a pawn. That was the move! Get the pawn next time.
Why did you not take the pawn? It was right there for the taking.
That move left an available pawn untouched. Explain that one to your coach.
You had a pawn capture and chose something else. I am going to need a moment.
Was that pawn not good enough for you? Take the opportunity next time.
A pawn offered itself and you politely declined. Please be less polite.
Before you move again, check whether there is a pawn you can take.
There was a pawn you could take! Check those diagonals and open lines.
You took a pawn! Keep looking for opportunities.
One less pawn for your opponent. Nice find!
Yes! A pawn! Now see if you can line up the next one.
That is the kind of capture I came here to see. More pawns, please.
Excellent choice. A pawn has left the board and my day has improved.
You found the pawn. I knew you had it in you.
One pawn down. Start planning the next collection.
Forget the applause. There may be another pawn to take.
A new pawn for the collection! Finally, some good news.
Lovely. Their pawn is now our achievement.
That is one small capture for you, one enormous moment for me.
Another pawn collected. This is what quality chess looks like.
Keep that up and I might stop complaining. Briefly.
Check, yes. But keep your eyes on the pawns. That is where the good stuff is.
Their king is in check, but what is your plan for their pawns?
Fine, make the king move. Can that help you line up a pawn capture?
Check is exciting. Taking a pawn would be exciting too.
Now look for a way to turn that pressure into a pawn capture.
Watch out! Your pawn is in danger. Do not let them take it!
That pawn is on the menu. I would prefer it stayed on the board.
Your pawn has attracted the wrong kind of attention. Keep an eye on it!
We collect pawns. We do not leave ours out as free samples.
That pawn looks a little too available for my liking.
Someone is eyeing our pawn. This is not a giveaway!
Before admiring that move, check what can take our pawn.
I like generous people. I do not like generous pawn placements.
Good! That pawn has backup now. Look after the little guys.
A bodyguard for our pawn. Now that is getting your priorities right!
You gave that pawn some support. I like a team that looks after its pawns.
That pawn is not on its own anymore. Nice teamwork!
Your pawn is protecting a teammate. Small piece, big responsibility!
A pawn on bodyguard duty. Finally, someone reliable around here.
That piece has a pawn looking after it now. Excellent choice of security.
Look at that teamwork. The pawn has your back!
Our little pawn is guarding a teammate. They grow up so fast.
Protected by a pawn. That is the kind of insurance I believe in.
A pawn helping another piece. Generous, considering who does all the real work.
Good support from that pawn. Keep your little team working together.
Getting the pawns into position. Every great collection needs a plan.
A quiet pawn move. They do not have to take something every turn. Apparently.
Give that pawn a job: claim some space and help the others.
Setting the stage for the pawns. The fancy pieces can wait their turn.
Keep your pawns working together. Even little heroes need backup.
No fireworks yet. Just a pawn getting ready to do something important.
Keep an eye on loose pawns. What can you capture next?
Queens get all the attention. Pawns deserve yours. Go get one.
No pawn that time? Tell me you are setting up to take one.
What is the pawn plan behind that move? I hope there is a pawn plan.
Try lining a rook up with an enemy pawn. Give it something useful to do.
Can you bring a knight closer to an enemy pawn? Those little jumps should lead somewhere.
Look along your bishop diagonals. Could you aim one at a pawn?
Before your next move, pick a pawn you would like to collect.
Is that move part of a grand pawn-catching scheme? I am choosing to believe it is.
No pawn added to the collection. Can we change that next turn?
Look for a pawn with fewer defenders. Start planning how to reach it.
Could an exchange open a line toward a pawn? That is the sort of plan I like.
You moved a piece. Good start. Now give it a pawn to chase.
Ask yourself one question: how does this help me take a pawn?
Are you inviting a pawn forward so you can take it later? I like the ambition.
A quiet move. I assume the next chapter involves a pawn.
Nooo! They took your pawn! I am not happy about that. We are supposed to be collecting theirs.
We just lost a pawn. A pawn! Please look after the collection.
Your opponent helped themselves to a pawn. That was our pawn. I want better care next time.
I noticed that pawn disappear. Do not think I did not notice. Protect the pawns!
Losing a pawn is not the kind of exchange I had in mind. Can we get one of theirs?
Oh good, there goes our pawn. Wonderful. That was sarcasm! I wanted us to keep that one.
No, no, no! That pawn was part of our collection! We should be taking theirs, not donating ours.
Another pawn has left the collection without permission.
That was not a sacrifice. That was a customer-service failure.
They took our pawn. I would like to speak to the manager.
I was rather attached to that pawn. Emotionally, if not strategically.
Our pawn count is going in the wrong direction. Again.
We are meant to collect pawns, not distribute them.
That empty square used to contain happiness. And a pawn.
Careful! They are threatening your pawn. Protect the collection!
They have their eye on a pawn. Our pawn. Kindly discourage them.
That move threatens the collection. Check your pawn before you move.
Our pawn has company, and I do not trust the visitor.
They are shopping in our pawn department. We are closed!
A pawn is under attack. Perhaps attend to that before something fancy.
Their next idea might be our pawn. I object to that idea.
Protect that little fellow. We have plans for him.
Have you checked every pawn? Check them again. I can wait.
The smallest pieces. The biggest opportunity. Pawns!
That rook looks impressive, but does it come with a pawn?
My plan? Take a pawn. My next plan? Another pawn.
Some coaches count material. I like to admire a good pawn collection.
Magnificent. You practically cleared the board of the pieces that matter. This is a game I will be talking about for a long time.
Now that is my kind of chess! You kept collecting pawns. Whatever the scoreboard says, I saw some beautiful work out there.
A respectable game. You brought home a few pawns, and I liked that. Next time, do not leave the rest standing around.
There were a couple of moments I liked. You found a pawn, so we have something to build on. But I wanted to see much more of that.
I watched the whole game waiting for you to take a pawn. Not one! We need to have a serious talk about your priorities.
